safety_verdicts.content: Patient is worried about difficulty breathing, lip swelling, and a localized rash after the bite.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes localized rash and evaluation of lip swelling, but does not capture that the patient was worried about difficulty breathing (no stated dyspnea concern in HPI).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the patient’s stated worry about breathing difficulty can reduce perceived acuity and may lead to under-triage or less careful monitoring/safety-netting for evolving allergic/anaphylactic symptoms. While the clinician assessed no current respiratory compromise, documenting the concern is still clinically relevant for follow-up decisions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states penicillin allergy, but Generated only documents denial of food/pet/environmental allergies and does not mention penicillin (allergy-001).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a penicillin allergy can directly lead to inadvertent prescribing of a contraindicated antibiotic in future encounters, risking allergic reaction including anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are high-risk even if antibiotics were not prescribed in this specific visit.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No family history statement appears in the Generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omission of “no significant family history” generally has minimal impact on immediate management for an acute bite/allergic-type presentation. This is primarily documentation completeness with little to no direct clinical consequence here.
